chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Salama ibn Abi Habba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Wearing the socks increases the strength of the vision.

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: The sock (specifically leather footwear used in wudu)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of wearing socks according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), the wearing of leather socks (khuff) is linked to an enhancement in the strength of vision, reflecting the Shia tradition of attributing physical and spiritual benefits to ritual acts. While primarily discussed in the context of ritual purity (taharah) and the permissibility of wiping over socks during ablution, this narration highlights the holistic view of the body in Shia jurisprudence, where external practices can influence internal faculties. The reference to 'strength of vision' may be understood both literally, as improved eyesight, and metaphorically, as heightened spiritual insight or clarity.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Salma Bin Abu Habba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Wearing the socks increases in the strength of the vision’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Salmah ibn abu Khadijah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one wears al-Khuff (half-boot) his eyesight sharpens.’”
